key_insight: CADRE is a frozen-backbone, parameter-efficient adaptation method that aims to improve medical VLM stability by reducing both forgetting of prior modalities and drift away from pretrained knowledge.
clinical_relevance: For clinical imaging systems, this could support safer adaptation to new modalities while better preserving performance on previously learned ones, but it is not a deployment guarantee.
method: Uses LoRA to adapt only a small fraction of parameters (~0.23%).
Adds an online, self-scaling, similarity-aware elastic weight consolidation term to limit forgetting.
Adds an anchor-to-prior penalty to keep embeddings close to the frozen pretrained model.
evidence_signal: In a multi-seed, multi-order breast cancer cross-modality stress test across histopathology, ultrasound, and chest radiography, CADRE showed the best accuracy, SPQ, and backward transfer and the lowest forgetting, with forgetting reduced from 0.075 to 0.011 versus the strongest regularized baseline (paired p=0.023).
watch_item: Results are from a controlled cross-modality setting; robustness to broader distribution shift and adversarial inputs was not evaluated.
paper_title: CADRE: Stable, Parameter Efficient Adaptation of Medical Vision Language Models with Bounded Forgetting and Prior Drift
